## 🔬 Major Technical Developments

### Making glass-to-metal seals for home­made vacuum tubes
URL: https://maurycyz.com/projects/glass/1/
Revival of foundational electronics manufacturing techniques outside industrial settings
Detailed walkthrough of creating hermetic seals for DIY vacuum tubes—a critical skill that's been locked inside specialized manufacturing for decades. Relevant for hardware hackers exploring alternatives to semiconductor supply chains and for understanding the physical limits of electronics fabrication.

### Show HN: Kage – Shadow any website to a single binary for offline viewing
URL: https://github.com/tamnd/kage
Single-binary website archival tool emerges as web preservation becomes increasingly urgent
Developer tool that captures entire websites into portable executables for offline access. Useful signal for enterprise compliance teams needing audit trails, researchers archiving ephemeral content, and anyone concerned about link rot and platform dependency.

## 💼 Business & Market Signals

### As AI companies race to go public, who else is along for the ride?
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/06/14/as-ai-companies-race-to-go-public-who-else-is-along-for-the-ride/
AI IPO pipeline creating liquidity opportunities across adjacent startups
Companies attempting to draft behind SpaceX's anticipated IPO momentum. Watch for secondary market activity in AI infrastructure plays and which late-stage names are accelerating timelines to catch the window before sentiment shifts.

### Meta reportedly moves to unwind $2B Manus deal after Beijing's demand
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/06/13/meta-reportedly-moves-to-unwind-2b-manus-deal-after-beijings-demand/
Beijing forces Meta to reverse $2B acquisition—cross-border M&A risk crystallizes
China ordering deal reversal sets precedent for retroactive regulatory intervention in tech M&A. Creates meaningful uncertainty for any Western tech company with Chinese exposure. Expect valuation haircuts on cross-border targets and extended diligence timelines.

### UK may ban social media for children under 16
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/06/14/uk-may-ban-social-media-for-children-under-16/
UK follows Australia with broad teen social media restrictions—regulatory contagion spreading
Second major Western democracy moving toward blanket bans rather than platform self-regulation. Meta, Snap, and TikTok face material DAU compression in key markets. Age verification infrastructure becomes a growth vertical.

## 📋 Case Studies & Deep Dives

### Startup CEO Charlie Javice is reportedly angling for a Trump pardon
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/06/14/startup-ceo-charlie-javice-is-reportedly-angling-for-a-trump-pardon/
Frank founder's pardon pursuit highlights JPMorgan's $175M acquisition due diligence failure
Javice, charged with fraud related to inflated user metrics in JPMorgan's Frank acquisition, now seeking political intervention. Case study in how acquirers can miss basic data verification. JPMorgan wrote down the entire investment; any pardon would be a PR disaster for the bank.

### As Anthropic suspends access to new models, India debates its AI future
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/06/13/as-anthropic-suspends-access-to-new-models-india-debates-its-ai-future/
Anthropic model access suspension forces India to confront AI sovereignty questions
India's tech leadership using the Anthropic access pause as catalyst for domestic AI development debate. Signals potential for India to accelerate sovereign AI initiatives—watch for policy announcements and whether Indian conglomerates (Reliance, Tata) increase AI infrastructure investment.

## ⚡ Signal vs. Noise

The Meta-Manus unwind is the week's clearest signal: geopolitical risk in tech M&A has shifted from theoretical to operational. Combined with the AI IPO frenzy, we're seeing a market that's simultaneously euphoric on domestic AI and repricing international exposure. The UK social media ban accelerates a regulatory pattern that will compress big tech's addressable market faster than most models anticipate.
